findings.text: Error message bug: both expectedFmt and actualFmt use expectedNames[i] instead of actualNames[i] for actualFmt, causing incorrect function names in mismatch reports when comparing functional options with different names.
Panic risk: tValue.Len() is called without checking reflect.Kind first; if f.value is not a slice/array/map/channel (e.g., a single function or nil), Len() will panic at runtime.
Panic risk: expectedOpts.Len() is called without verifying expectedOpts.Kind() is Slice/Array/Map/Chan; passing a non-slice to FunctionalOptions comparison will panic.
Logic bug: when tValue.Len() == 0, the type check is skipped entirely, allowing type mismatches between expected and actual functional options to go undetected if the expected slice is empty.

0.reason: The actualFmt uses expectedNames[i] instead of actualNames[i], which is a direct manifestation of the reference bug where equal options from indirect calls get different names and compare unequal.

1.reason: tValue.Len() is called without checking reflect.Kind, so if f.value is not a slice/array/map/channel, it will panic at runtime.

2.reason: expectedOpts.Len() is called without verifying expectedOpts.Kind() is Slice/Array/Map/Chan, so passing a non-slice to FunctionalOptions comparison will panic.

3.reason: When tValue.Len() == 0, the type check is skipped, but this is intentional because an empty slice has no type information to compare, and the code handles it by falling through to the else branch.
